title: SAC Jet Drops 500-Pound Bombs on Khawpuichhip and Zimpi Villages in Falam Township — 5 Children and 1 Man Killed Near India Border; 150+ Refugees Flee to Mizoram
detail: A Myanmar junta jet fighter from Tada-U Air Base dropped two 500-pound bombs on Khawpuichhip village (approximately 5 km from the Mizoram/India border) and Zimpi village in the Hualngoram area of Falam Township, Chin State, on May 1, 2026 — killing five children aged 3 to 10 years and one man aged 29, injuring at least 10 others, and destroying 15–20 buildings. The junta also burned Thlanrawn village in Falam Township the same afternoon. The strikes near the Indian border triggered a fresh wave of civilian displacement: more than 150 villagers fled across the border into Zokhawthar, Champhai District, Mizoram, adding to the approximately 30,000 Myanmar refugees already sheltering in India's northeast states. The Khawpuichhip/Zimpi strikes are part of the SAC's ongoing air campaign in Chin State following its April 25-26 recapture of Falam town — a campaign that also included the April 30 Kanpetlet bridge construction site strike (9 workers killed) and a pattern of post-recapture aerial punishment in surrounding villages. The proximity to the Indian border and the confirmed refugee influx into Mizoram threatens to escalate bilateral tensions between India and Myanmar on humanitarian grounds. MoeMaKa CDM News and Northeast Live TV documented the strike; Aryan Age reported the refugee influx into Champhai District.

media.caption: SAC jet bombs Khawpuichhip and Zimpi villages near India-Myanmar border (Falam Township, Chin State): 5 children and 1 man killed, 150+ refugees flee to Mizoram, May 1, 2026

title: Aung San Suu Kyi Transferred from Naypyidaw Prison to House Arrest — NUG and Son Kim Aris Reject Move as 'Deceptive Maneuver,' Demand Proof of Life
detail: Myanmar state media (MRTV) announced on April 30, 2026 that former State Counsellor and Nobel Peace Laureate Aung San Suu Kyi had been transferred from Naypyidaw Prison to house arrest — an announcement confirmed by the junta on May 1, 2026. The transfer ends more than five years of near-total isolation at the high-security military prison. Her sentence was previously reduced to approximately 22.5 years on April 17 via a general amnesty. The NUG Acting President Duwa Lashi La and other officials immediately rejected the announcement as a 'deceptive political maneuver' by newly inaugurated President Min Aung Hlaing aimed at rehabilitating Myanmar's international image. Suu Kyi's son Kim Aris issued an urgent statement demanding credible proof that his mother is alive, noting that her lawyers had not been able to verify the transfer independently. Diaspora protesters in Washington D.C. demonstrated outside the Myanmar Embassy demanding proof of life. Canada had reaffirmed recognition of U Win Myint as Myanmar's legitimate president on April 23, calling for the release of Suu Kyi and all political prisoners. NPR reported the transfer in the context of the junta's broader image-burnishing campaign following the April 10 presidential inauguration — widely seen as a domestic propaganda exercise rather than genuine political liberalization.

media.caption: Myanmar junta transfers Aung San Suu Kyi from Naypyidaw Prison to house arrest — NUG and son Kim Aris demand proof of life, reject move as political manipulation, May 1, 2026

title: Junta Forces Invade Yinmabin, Pale, and Kani Townships in Lower Sagaing — Large SAC Columns Enter Following Bo Nagar's Surrender
detail: Myanmar military junta forces launched a renewed ground offensive into Yinmabin Township, Pale Township, and Kani Township in lower Sagaing Region on May 1, 2026, deploying large SAC columns that triggered local battles with PDF and resistance forces throughout the area. Mizzima's Spring Revolution Daily News (May 1) reported the invasion as a significant escalation in the three townships. The offensive is linked to the April 2026 surrender of resistance commander Bo Nagar, whose defection reportedly provided the junta with intelligence on PDF positions and command structures in the lower Sagaing area, enabling the concentrated push. Yinmabin Township had already seen resistance operations in April 2026, including the April 27 landmine ambush that killed 3 SAC troops near Telpinkhan village; the junta's May 1 invasion represents a large-scale counter-offensive attempting to re-establish SAC presence in the area. Kani Township has been an active PDF stronghold with sustained resistance ambushes against SAC convoys throughout 2026. The coordinated simultaneous invasion of three adjacent townships suggests a deliberate encirclement strategy against PDF forces in the lower Sagaing pocket rather than isolated punitive raids.

media.caption: SAC launches large-scale invasion of Yinmabin, Pale, and Kani townships (lower Sagaing Region) on May 1, 2026 — coordinated multi-township offensive following Bo Nagar's surrender
